summary: Frontend-only validation of iteration 55 SEO round: (a) 16 OG hero images resized to 1200x630 landscape and (b) 20 thin blog posts expanded via LLM. All 5 sampled expanded articles render correctly (single H1, 6-10 H2s, bullet+numbered lists, bold, closing italic CTA blockquote, correct breadcrumbs, no raw ## or ** leaking). All 16 -og.jpg files verified locally and via CDN as exactly 1200x630, quality-82 JPEG (~67-70KB). og:image meta on /services/managed-it-services and /ai-readiness-assessment correctly points to the -og.jpg filenames. /resources index shows refreshed 1-sentence excerpts and 5-7 min read-time labels for the updated posts. Untouched post ai-cybersecurity-threats-2025 still has original short content (2586 chars, unchanged). Homepage, service page, AI page, and Saint Paul city page (/service-areas/st-paul-mn) all render with proper titles + H1 and no functional regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: Pre-existing (not introduced this iteration): a benign 'Unexpected token <' pageerror fires on many prerendered routes (services, AI, blog posts, city pages) - it does not affect rendering. Likely a background source-map or hashed-chunk 404 during hydration. Worth investigating in a future iteration but is outside the scope of this OG-image + blog-expansion round.

3 category OG images (construction-category-hero-og.jpg, financial-services-category-hero-og.jpg, manufacturing-category-hero-og.jpg) remain 1024x1024 - explicitly out of scope per the request (only 5 core-service + 11 AI-page = 16 images were in scope), noting for future SEO round if category pages also emit og:image.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_55 validated OG image landscape resize (16 files) and 20 blog-post expansions. All served correctly. If future rounds expand the remaining 109 thin posts, reuse the same 5-point check per post: single H1, multiple H2s, at least one list, bold, and a closing italic CTA rendered as border-l blockquote (p.italic with border-l-2). Blog data endpoint pattern: /api/blog/{slug}. City page pattern is /service-areas/{slug} (not /managed-it-services-{slug}).
